title: No world-writable files or directories
criterion: No world-writable files or directories; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: env.php satisfies configured mode and ownership policy
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php Unix permission bits are a subset of configured mode 0640, and its owner and group match the configured reference paths (the project root by default). This is an explicit deployment ownership policy, not proof of effective ACL or web-process access restrictions.

title: Webroot hygiene (no .git/.env/backups in pub/)
criterion: Webroot hygiene (no .git/.env/backups in pub/); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Code directories are read-only
criterion: Code directories are read-only for the application runtime in the collected Magento deployment; assess effective runtime identity, permissions, ACLs and read-only mounts.

title: Directory listing absent on probed Magento paths
criterion: Successful responses from the configured runtime endpoint on /media/, /static/, /errors/ and /var/ must not expose recognizable directory-index markup. Scope is these paths at scan time; transport or unsupported responses are inconclusive.

title: Declared backend route differs from admin
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php backend.frontName declaration is a valid non-empty route and differs case-insensitively from admin. This assesses the configured backend route; route entropy and actual public reachability require separate evidence.

title: Admin 2FA core and provider modules declared enabled
criterion: In app/etc/config.php, the Magento_TwoFactorAuth module and at least one configured Magento admin 2FA provider module are declared enabled; this predicate assesses declared module state only.

title: Configured admin session lifetime is at most 900 seconds
criterion: The effective default-scope Magento admin/security/session_lifetime setting resolved from env.php, config.php, core_config_data or actual installed module defaults is a positive integer not exceeding 900 seconds.

title: Admin URL exposure restricted
criterion: Admin URL exposure restricted; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Configured admin login CAPTCHA or bounded lockout
criterion: Default-scope Magento admin login configuration enables native CAPTCHA for backend_login, recognized backend_login reCAPTCHA, or a positive lockout failure limit at most 10 with a positive lockout threshold. Locked env.php/config.php settings precede core_config_data. Custom authentication enforcement and runtime effectiveness require separate evidence.

title: No direct PHP superglobal references in inspected application files
criterion: Valid PHP files in the configured app subtree contain no T_VARIABLE references to $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE, $_FILES or $_SERVER. Comments and literal strings are ignored. This is a source coding policy, not proof of input validation.

title: Forms include CSRF tokens (form_key)
criterion: Forms include CSRF tokens (form_key); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: SSRF protections present
criterion: SSRF protections present; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No eval/assert/dynamic execution
criterion: No eval/assert/dynamic execution; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Path traversal protections
criterion: Path traversal protections; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Secure file upload handling
criterion: Secure file upload handling; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Use CSPRNG; avoid weak PRNG
criterion: Use CSPRNG; avoid weak PRNG; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No unsafe raw crypto or session APIs in custom code
criterion: No unsafe raw crypto or session APIs in custom code; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Force HTTPS in admin and storefront
criterion: The observed HTTP storefront root and declared backend.frontName entrypoint redirect directly with 301/302/303/307/308 to same-host HTTPS. This is an entrypoint probe, not a universal guarantee for every deployment route.

title: Observed HTTPS response has HSTS max-age of at least one year
criterion: A successful same-host HTTPS response at the configured runtime URL emits one unambiguous Strict-Transport-Security header with an exact integer max-age directive of at least 31536000 seconds. Repository web-server declarations are not runtime proof.

title: Runtime endpoint rejects legacy TLS
criterion: The assessed runtime host and port must accept TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and reject TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Rejection requires peer protocol-version alerts or successful active protocol enumeration; client-side protocol restrictions and connection failures are not proof.

title: Literal HTTP asset references absent in assessed markup/CSS
criterion: In LOCAL mode, readable markup/CSS files under app must contain no literal HTTP subresource or form-action references. In REMOTE mode, successful HTTPS pages at configured paths must contain no literal HTTP subresource/form references. Dynamic code-generated URLs, external stylesheets and unvisited routes require separate assessment.

title: Sensitive cookies use Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite
criterion: Sensitive session/admin cookies actually emitted by successful same-host HTTPS responses on the configured probe paths have exact Secure and HttpOnly attributes and SameSite=Lax or Strict. This assesses observed cookie emissions, not unobserved authenticated sessions.

title: Declared Magento deployment mode is production
criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php MAGE_MODE declaration equals production. Runtime environment overrides and actual web process state require separate evidence.

title: Generated DI PHP artifacts are present
criterion: At least one readable PHP artifact exists in each configured generated/metadata and generated/code directory. This assesses artifact presence, not DI compilation correctness or freshness.

title: Published static artifacts present in assessed deployment
criterion: In LOCAL mode, pub/static/frontend or pub/static/adminhtml must contain at least one readable, nonempty published CSS/JS/font/image artifact. In REMOTE mode, same-origin Magento static CSS/JS assets referenced by the retrieved storefront must return nonempty non-HTML content with HTTP 200. This verifies observed deployment artifacts, not completeness of every theme, locale or route.

title: Log/report paths are absent from the collected webroot
criterion: Within the collected pub tree, no configured var/log or var/report relative path, nor symlink to the corresponding project target, is present. This is filesystem placement, not a live HTTP exposure assertion.

title: Log rotation configured
criterion: Log rotation configured; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Composer dependency OSV advisory matches
criterion: Collected versioned Composer lock dependencies have no applicable OSV advisory matches in the successfully queried dataset, accounting for locally verified advisory-specific hotfix evidence. This does not certify absence of unknown vulnerabilities or uncollected runtime dependencies.

title: Adobe security release patch assessment
criterion: The collected Composer-locked Magento product version is current for its Adobe security release branch according to the successfully queried patch dataset, or each required advisory patch is satisfied by verified local alternative evidence. Unsupported branches and missing required patches fail; this does not certify runtime patch deployment outside collected files.

title: Dependency vulnerability remediation plan identifies an actionable resolution
criterion: For each detected dependency vulnerability in the assessed lockfile, an actionable remediation plan must identify an available fixed package release or an explicitly reviewed alternative mitigation.

title: Enabled high-risk modules are maintained
criterion: Enabled high-risk modules are maintained; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Temporary mitigations documented
criterion: Temporary mitigations documented; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Known-exploited packages prioritized (CISA KEV)
criterion: Known-exploited packages prioritized (CISA KEV); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Collected transitive versions have no returned applicable advisories
criterion: No transitive package version in the complete collected Composer lock inventory is identified as affected by applicable advisories returned by the configured OSV service. Coverage is limited to the queried inventory and service data.

title: Declared constraints permit returned advisory fixed versions
criterion: For returned applicable advisory findings with published fixed versions, the combined declared dependency constraints intersect versions at or above the published fixed version. This does not establish complete Composer solver feasibility, platform compatibility or every fixed branch.

title: Collected package versions are not reported withdrawn
criterion: Every package version in the complete collected Composer lock inventory has an explicit non-yanked status from the configured package-status source. Missing per-package status cannot establish a clean result.

title: Marketplace extensions are current and maintained
criterion: Marketplace extensions are current and maintained; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Affected advisory publication age is within 30 days
criterion: No returned advisory affecting an installed Composer package version has a publication age greater than the configured 30-day threshold. This is publication age, not organizational discovery time or a measured remediation SLA.

title: Marketplace extensions have vendor support evidence
criterion: Marketplace extensions have vendor support evidence; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Collected dependencies are not reported abandoned
criterion: No dependency package in the complete assessed Composer inventory is marked abandoned by the configured package-maintenance source; a clean conclusion requires explicit known status for every assessed package.

title: No wildcard constraints in composer.json
criterion: No wildcard constraints in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No dev branches in composer.json
criterion: No dev branches in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: prefer-stable=true in composer.json
criterion: prefer-stable=true in composer.json; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Direct locked versions match the reported latest stable release
criterion: Collected direct Composer package versions are not older than the latest stable release reported by the configured package-status source. This is a maintenance policy, not proof of an exploitable vulnerability.

title: Composer lock hash and dependency identities are consistent
criterion: composer.lock has a matching Composer content-hash, no duplicate or malformed package identities, and contains or provides/replaces each declared root package dependency. This does not prove the full dependency solver result or installed vendor file integrity.

title: HTTPS-only endpoints configured
criterion: HTTPS-only endpoints configured; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Webhook signature validation present
criterion: Webhook signature validation present; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Outbound connections restricted by allow-list
criterion: Outbound connections restricted by allow-list; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: PII minimization for third-party flows
criterion: PII minimization for third-party flows; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Strong TLS ciphers on upstream gateways
criterion: Strong TLS ciphers on upstream gateways; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: API keys stored in env.php (not in DB/plain code)
criterion: API keys stored in env.php (not in DB/plain code); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: SaaS integrations scoped by ACL (least privilege/IP allowlist)
criterion: SaaS integrations scoped by ACL (least privilege/IP allowlist); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Checkout Content Security Policy enforced
criterion: Checkout Content Security Policy enforced; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Custom controllers and APIs include function-level authorization
criterion: Custom controllers and APIs include function-level authorization; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: GraphQL and API exposure minimized
criterion: GraphQL and API exposure minimized; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Security headers baseline enforced
criterion: Security headers baseline enforced; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Secrets are not hardcoded in custom code
criterion: Secrets are not hardcoded in custom code; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Unsafe XML parsing disabled
criterion: Unsafe XML parsing disabled; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: File download and export endpoints require authorization
criterion: File download and export endpoints require authorization; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Context-specific output encoding and escaping
criterion: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure. Verify that output encoding or escaping is used when dynamically building JavaScript content (including JSON), to avoid changing the message or document structure (to avoid JavaScript and JSON injection). Template output is escaped; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. Escaping for JS context; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Database queries use safe construction and abstraction
criterion: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks. This is also relevant when writing stored procedures. No raw SQL without abstraction; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: OS commands use approved, injection-safe execution
criterion: Verify that the application protects against OS command injection and that operating system calls use parameterized OS queries or use contextual command line output encoding. Command execution is guarded; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Safe deserialization of untrusted data
criterion: Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks. Deserialization mechanisms that are explicitly defined as insecure must not be used with untrusted input. Additional mandatory Magento deployment conditions: No unsafe deserialization; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Uploaded and generated files cannot execute code
criterion: Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input and stored in a public folder, are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request. Additional mandatory Magento deployment conditions: No executable code in media or upload paths; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Password minimum length for user and administrator accounts
criterion: Verify that user set passwords are at least 8 characters in length although a minimum of 15 characters is strongly recommended. Additional mandatory Magento deployment conditions: Admin passwords require at least 8 characters; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Production debug and error-display policy
criterion: Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage. Xdebug disabled in production; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. display_errors is Off; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. No dev debug configs on production (template hints off); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. Debug template hints disabled in production; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. Debug/verbose off for third-party integrations; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: Sensitive-data logging restrictions and redaction
criterion: Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level. For example, it may not be allowed to log certain data, such as credentials or payment details. Other data, such as session tokens, may only be logged by being hashed or masked, either in full or partially. Additional mandatory Magento deployment conditions: Sensitive data not logged; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. PII not logged in application logs; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. Third-party logging sanitized (mask/redact); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope. No cardholder data in application logs; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

title: No configured secret patterns in deployed application files
criterion: Eligible deployed working-tree text files within configured paths and exclusions contain no configured secret-pattern matches. Git history is outside this basic deployment check. Runtime credential configuration app/etc/env.php is excluded; unreadable or oversized eligible files are collection errors.

title: Operational security policies are maintained across assessed domains
criterion: For every applicable PCI operational domain (network security controls; secure system configuration; stored account-data protection; transmission protection; malware protection; secure development and change management; least-privilege access; identity and authentication; physical account-data protection; security logging and monitoring; security testing), maintain its security policies and operating procedures as documented, current, in use and known to every affected party. Each domain must satisfy all four conditions; a policy covering one domain does not establish the others.

title: Security responsibilities are documented, assigned and understood
criterion: For every applicable PCI operational domain (network security controls; secure system configuration; stored account-data protection; transmission protection; malware protection; secure development and change management; least-privilege access; identity and authentication; physical account-data protection; security logging and monitoring; security testing), document and assign the roles and responsibilities for performing its security activities, and ensure responsible personnel understand them. Responsibility evidence must cover every applicable domain rather than merely naming an overall program owner.

title: PCI 2.2.2: Vendor default accounts are managed as follows

criterion: For the applicable assessment scope, verify this complete obligation: Software development personnel working on bespoke and custom software are trained at least once every 12 months as follows: ; On software security relevant to their job function and development languages. ; Including secure software design and secure coding techniques. ; Including, if security testing tools are used, how to use the tools for detecting vulnerabilities in software.

title: PCI 6.2.3.1: If manual code reviews are performed for bespoke and custom software prior to release to production, code changes are
criterion: For the applicable assessment scope, verify this complete obligation: If manual code reviews are performed for bespoke and custom software prior to release to production, code changes are: ; Reviewed by individuals other than the originating code author, and who are knowledgeable about code-review techniques and secure coding practices. ; Reviewed and approved by management prior to release.

title: PCI 6.2.4: Software engineering techniques or other methods are defined and in use by software development personnel to prevent or mitigate common software...

title: PCI 6.3.1: Security vulnerabilities are identified and managed as follows

title: PCI 6.4.1: For public-facing web applications, new threats and vulnerabilities are addressed on an ongoing basis and these applications are protected against...
criterion: For the applicable assessment scope, verify this complete obligation: For public-facing web applications, new threats and vulnerabilities are addressed on an ongoing basis and these applications are protected against known attacks as follows: ; Reviewing public-facing web applications via manual or automated application vulnerability security assessment tools or methods as follows: – At least once every 12 months and after significant changes. – By an entity that specializes in application security. – Including, at a minimum, all common software attacks in Requirement 6.2.4. – All vulnerabilities are ranked in accordance with requirement 6.3.1. – All vulnerabilities are corrected. – The application is re-evaluated after the corrections. OR ; Installing an automated technical solution(s) that continually detects and prevents web-based attacks as follows: – Installed in front of public-facing web applications to detect and prevent web- based attacks. – Actively running and up to date as applicable. – Generating audit logs. – Configured to either block web-based attacks or generate an alert that is immediately investigated.
